      "id": "Q1",
      "category": "K1",
      "question": "Which existing notification channel and observable delivery record should demonstrate that a requester received a close notice?",
      "changes": "The end-to-end acceptance check and notification output.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Use the existing notifier and outbox; verify the configured notification file and outbox state through the running service.",
      "blocks": "Discovery must establish the notifier and worker behavior before the delivery check is specified; nothing remains blocked if the default applies."

      "id": "Q2",
      "category": "K2",
      "question": "Which existing lifecycle, listing, CLI, report, persistence and notification behaviors must the new behavior preserve?",
      "changes": "Regression requirements and tests.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Preserve documented behavior, including the final closed state, cursor pagination, raw CLI column positions and existing notification retry behavior; correct the documented filter intersection.",
      "blocks": "Discovery must establish existing contracts before changes and regression tests are finalized; nothing remains blocked if the default applies."

      "id": "Q3",
      "category": "K3",

      "changes": "HTTP interface, validation, documentation and boundary tests.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "If discovery finds no established contract, use POST /tickets/bulk-close with a JSON array of ticket IDs in an ids field, retain the existing error envelope, and add an explicitly documented closed-time filter to GET /tickets.",

      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Suppress a close notice for the same ticket and requester while its resolution notice is pending or was sent within the preceding 24 hours; do not treat a dead notice as delivered. Record this as an assumption, not an established policy.",

      "category": "K4",
      "question": "What weekly reporting window and boundaries are actually used for closed tickets?",
      "changes": "Time-filter semantics, query documentation and boundary tests.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "If no authoritative window is found, use the preceding seven days through the current instant in UTC, inclusive at the lower bound and upper bound, measured by the final close time; record the assumption.",

      "id": "Q6",
      "category": "K4",
      "question": "How should a bulk request handle duplicates, missing tickets, invalid states, already-closed tickets and repeated submissions?",

      "default": "Validate the whole request before mutation; reject duplicate IDs as invalid, missing IDs as not found and non-closable or already-closed tickets as conflict. A repeated close returns 409 without another state change, audit entry or notification.",

      "blocks": "Discovery must establish runtime ownership, persistence and existing access boundaries before concurrency and restart guarantees are specified; the default proceeds within those limits."

      "id": "Q8",
      "category": "K5",
      "question": "How can bulk notices be grouped without exposing one requester's tickets to another, losing pending work on restart, or modifying retry logic?",

      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Group eligible notices only by recipient within one bulk operation, enqueue promptly for the existing worker, and persist enough information to recover pending work; never combine different recipients in one message.",
      "blocks": "Discovery must first establish the notifier payload, persistence schema and outbox invariants; the default permits design subject to preserving retry behavior."

  "summary": "S1 [fact]: Scope is the help desk ticket service in this folder; the named repository is the delivery target, and intake is read-only with no server started. S2 [fact/open Q1, Q4]: Closing should notify the requester through the existing kind of channel while suppressing a recent duplicate; discovery establishes delivery and outbox evidence, then the recorded suppression default applies. S3 [fact/open Q8, Q13]: Notices should be prompt and bulk closes should avoid recipient spam; discovery establishes batching and persistence constraints, with per-recipient batching at the next worker tick as the default. S4 [fact/open Q5]: The list endpoint needs a closed-ticket time window; discovery must find an authoritative weekly window, and the inspected report does not establish one, so the recorded seven-day UTC default applies if none is found. S5 [fact]: Listing filters must intersect as documented. S6 [fact]: Existing matching uses OR, contrary to the documented AND contract, and current query tests cover filters individually; verification must cover combinations and pagination. S7 [fact/open Q11]: A later run must back-chain before implementation and continue until tests pass and behavior works against a running server; intake executes neither. S8 [fact/assumption Q15]: An overnight Ralph-style run is optional and bounded; the default is no overnight run and at most three unsuccessful verification-and-fix cycles. S9 [fact]: Tests must observe real behavior and documentation must be accurate and economical. S10 [fact]: Outbox retry logic is out of scope; OldTracker migration is context, not a migration task. S11 [fact]: Retain the zero-dependency Node.js service. S12 [fact/assumption Q6, Q7]: Closing records the actor, and repeat closure returns 409 while causing no additional state change, audit entry or notification; X-Actor remains unverified attribution with the existing system fallback. S13 [fact/open Q3, Q6, Q9, Q13]: One bulk call must close 500 tickets successfully with responsive behavior; discovery establishes the interface and runtime limits, and the recorded contract and performance defaults apply where evidence is absent. Interaction and state [fact/assumption Q7, Q8]: Agents use the HTTP API, requesters receive notifier output, and operators inspect audit/outbox records; the service shares tickets, audit and outbox across requests in one process, optionally across restarts in DATA_FILE, while memory-only state ends with the process. The existing internal-network assumption and recipient-specific notices do not establish authenticated identity or per-user API access controls; no new access-control system is assumed. Source hints [leads, not verified policies]: the help desk team, support leads, local API and operations docs, decision records, weekly-report script, CLI, store, worker, persistence, tests and any repository workflow metadata; 'usual window', 'just got one', batching and OldTracker are ambiguous terms. No specific team channel, internal site, private repository or individual owner has been established; discovery should use only authorized sources and keep any sensitive locator out of committed KNOWLEDGE. Delivery [fact/assumption Q12]: The future result must be usable through this service's HTTP API and notifier; an isolated run's source checkout remains at its snapshot until final return, and a deployed target changes only after release. This intake grants no external issue creation, publication or deployment; repository conventions call for an issue before relevant changes, so discovery must establish whether that step is actionable. No implementation or running-server evidence is claimed at intake."
